output.summary: KEP-4210 adds an optional Kubelet setting, ImageMaximumGCAge, plus a feature gate, so that images unused for a set time are garbage collected regardless of disk usage. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Kubelet image GC only runs when disk usage crosses a threshold, so images from an old release (e.g. after an automatic upgrade) can sit on disk until then. The KEP adds an age-based trigger, defaulting to 0 (disabled), and the sources say it is opt-in and best-effort. Maintainers also raised reliability concerns, and sergeykanzhelev asked that the setting be explicitly documented as best effort; the sources do not record how those were resolved beyond the implemented status.

alternatives.option: Add a Kubelet garbage collection plugin system
alternatives.why_not: Too complicated, probably won't be needed.

alternatives.option: Delegate image GC responsibility down to CRI
alternatives.why_not: Would cause code duplication between CRI implementations, out of scope for this.

alternatives.option: Make ImageMinimumGCAge independent of the disk usage threshold
alternatives.why_not: ImageGCMinimumAge is only relevant under disk pressure, and ImageMaximumGCAge seeks to qualify otherwise unqualified images; the authors found the distinction clear, and the backwards compatibility issues were judged not worth the config size savings.

alternatives.option: Skip the alpha phase and go directly to beta
alternatives.why_not: Raised by kannon92 as a question; the sources do not record a decision on it beyond the KEP being added with a feature gate.

evidence.quote: An additional approach is to define a way for an admin to request images are cleaned up after they're unused for a certain period of time.
To begin, this option will be set to 0, which will be interpreted as "disabled". In the future, a more reasonable default may be chosen.
afaict we still require a feature gate, even for optional fields like this one.
we should clearly state the best effort nature of this setting than - it will simplify the design.
One direction to go is to allow more granular configuration on what falls under this policy and what is not.
